daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo has conducted six cabinet reshuffles in two years, prompting observers to question what the president is seeking through such frequent changes. Separately, Prabowo announced that 328 state-owned enterprises have been closed, claiming budget savings of Rp 50 trillion. The president also revealed that the new University of Rakyat Indonesia (URI) will oversee LAN and other governance academies, and said he established URI after citing concerns about a "deep state."

  • Coalition party leaders discussed raising the parliamentary threshold to 5 percent, which would have resulted in 17 million votes being wasted in the 2024 election, while observers predict DPR parties will approve the increase.
  • The Constitutional Court ruled on the free nutritious meals budget in the state budget (APBN).
  • Prabowo stated that former campaign team member Dadan was handed over to prosecutors by himself.
  • Minister Hasan Nasbi referenced Prabowo's past dismissal from the TNI during remarks about cabinet reshuffles.
  • Finance Minister Suahasil is studying the controversy over official rotations from the Purbaya era at the Finance Ministry after the Tax Director General proposed postponing rotations.
  • Former Babel Deputy Governor Hellyana returned to duty after being released from prison.
  • A corruption investigation exposed a "shadow structure" in land rights bribes at the Agrarian Ministry involving confidants of Minister Nusron, while former official Fahd Arafiq faces his third corruption case.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The United States is encouraging Indonesia to serve as a role model for Science, Technology and Mathematics (STM) development across ASEAN. President Prabowo reaffirmed Indonesia's commitment to a free and active foreign policy, stating the country will not join any bloc and will be friendly with all nations. Indonesia has also begun negotiations on nuclear goods within the STM framework.

  • Indonesia and Canada are targeting implementation of the ICA-CEPA trade agreement by late 2026.
  • Indonesia outlined its energy roadmap at a G20 meeting in Texas.
  • Indonesia is seeking to strengthen trade and cultural cooperation in border regions with neighboring countries, with the border agency (BNPP) partnering with neighbors to develop these areas.
  • Indonesia and Ireland are collaborating to develop AI for the aviation industry.
  • Indonesian Ambassador to China Djauhari stated that Indonesia-China diplomacy must benefit the people.

Other

President Prabowo and Jakarta Governor Pramono Anung jointly inaugurated the LRT expansion from Kelapa Gading to Manggarai, which strengthens public transport integration in the capital. Governor Pramono directly asked President Prabowo for assistance in extending LRT routes. Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said the new line reinforces inter-modal integration across Jakarta.

  • The government will prepare 2 million hectares of sugarcane land for the E20 ethanol program, targeting E20 production within two years.
  • President Prabowo ordered an investigation into the KMP Virgo Transport 8 accident, demanding families' rights be fulfilled, while the Transport Ministry will investigate whether the vessel was seaworthy and Basarnas is bringing in foreign salvage experts.
  • President Prabowo emphasized the Giant Sea Wall project to protect Java's northern coast and demanded perpetrators of forest fires be charged with "ecological terrorism".
  • The government plans to electrify 10,068 locations by 2029, reaching 770,000 households, with 4,602 remote sites using renewable energy, while a senior official said the electrification program could triple household incomes.
  • Labor unions expressed deep disappointment over the draft Labor Law revision, threatening large-scale demonstrations.
